reason: Rapid next x5 in 85 ms against 600-900 ms is a gap I would feel when I run through hundreds of RAW+JPG frames, and Windows Photos is the slowest thing I own at that. It is free and portable, so I lose nothing by trying it on a real shoot folder.
why_switch_or_not: A few tens of ms on a single open means nothing to me, but next/back at 40-50 ms and a fast burst of next presses is exactly what culling is. RAW and JPG showing as separate pictures is what I want, and it can read RAW from sensor data or the embedded preview. I would switch if my own RAW files flip as fast as the benchmark claims; the list says nothing about ratings, flags or delete-to-reject keys, so I would still check how I mark keepers before I trust it as the only viewer.
current_app_pros: It is already there and opens when I double-click. It handles ordinary JPGs fine and I never had to set anything up.
current_app_pains: It is slow to open and slow between pictures, and it lags noticeably when I hold the arrow key through a folder of RAW files. With 200,000 pictures spread over 15 years, anything that stalls on a big folder wastes my time every day.
objection: The benchmark is one PC, and it uses typical JPG/PNG, not my big RAW files from a big folder on a slow drive. It is also 0.4.1 from one man, and I do not see culling features like ratings or flags listed. If he stops working on it, I am back to Photos.
would_change_my_mind: Seeing it flip through a 2,000-file RAW+JPG folder on my own machine with no stall, and finding that I can reject or keep frames without leaving the viewer.
